actors.name: Project Manager
actors.description: Owns project setup, budget oversight, task planning, change orders, and status reporting for one or more jobs.

actors.name: Field Worker
actors.description: Receives assigned work tasks and records daily time and progress from the field (mobile-friendly).

actors.name: Billing Staff
actors.description: Prepares and reviews client billing summaries and invoices from approved job cost and change-order data.

actors.name: Client
actors.description: External customer who receives project status communication and billing summaries; limited self-serve visibility.

journeys.title: Create a new construction project
journeys.goal: Set up a new project with client information, site address, budget, and schedule so the team can start planning work.

steps.title: Enter project basics
steps.intent: The project manager enters the project name, selects or creates the client record, and fills in the site address so the project is properly identified and located.

steps.title: Set budget and schedule
steps.intent: The project manager defines the project budget and target start and end dates so cost tracking and scheduling have a baseline.

steps.title: Activate the project
steps.intent: The project manager confirms the project status is active so tasks, time logs, and materials can begin being recorded against it.

journeys.outcome: A new project exists with client, address, budget, schedule, and active status, ready for task planning and field work.
businessRules: A project must have a name, client, and site address before it can be activated.
Budget and schedule dates are required to begin job costing tracking.
Project status controls whether field entries can be recorded against the project.

journeys.title: Plan and assign work tasks for a project
journeys.goal: Break the project into actionable work tasks, assign them to field workers, and review the timeline so the crew knows what to do and when.

steps.title: Create work tasks
steps.intent: The project manager creates work tasks with descriptions tied to the project so the scope of work is broken into manageable units.

steps.title: Assign tasks with due dates
steps.intent: The project manager assigns each task to a field worker and sets a due date so the worker knows their responsibilities and deadlines.

steps.title: Review task timeline
steps.intent: The project manager reviews the task list and simple Gantt-ish timeline to confirm sequencing and dates make sense for the project schedule.

journeys.outcome: Work tasks are created, assigned to field workers with due dates, and visible in a timeline view for schedule coordination.
businessRules: Tasks must belong to an active project.
A task can only be assigned to one field worker at a time.
Due dates should fall within the project schedule window.

journeys.title: Review operational dashboard
journeys.goal: Get a quick overview of all active projects, spot budget drift, and identify upcoming or overdue tasks.

steps.title: View active projects
steps.intent: The project manager opens the dashboard to see all active projects at a glance so they know where attention is needed.

steps.title: Check budget vs actual
steps.intent: The project manager reviews budget versus actual cost signals for each project to spot jobs that are drifting over budget.

steps.title: Identify upcoming and overdue tasks
steps.intent: The project manager scans upcoming and overdue tasks across projects so they can reassign or reprioritize work before problems escalate.

journeys.outcome: The project manager has a clear picture of project health, budget status, and task urgency across all active jobs.
businessRules: Dashboard shows only active projects by default.
Budget vs actual is derived from labor time logs, material usage, and approved change orders.
Overdue tasks are highlighted based on due date comparison.

journeys.title: Create and approve a change order
journeys.goal: Document a scope, cost, or schedule change on an active project and apply its cost impact to the job.

steps.title: Document the change
steps.intent: The project manager creates a change order describing the scope, cost, or schedule adjustment so the change is formally captured rather than lost.

steps.title: Review cost impact
steps.intent: The project manager reviews how the change order affects the project budget so they understand the financial consequence before approving.

steps.title: Approve and apply the change
steps.intent: The project manager approves the change order so the adjusted cost and schedule are reflected in the project's job costing and billing data.

journeys.outcome: An approved change order adjusts the project's scope, cost, or schedule and flows into job costing and billing summaries.
businessRules: Change orders can only be created on active projects.
Only approved change orders affect job costing and billing.
A change order must describe the scope, cost, or schedule impact.

journeys.title: Generate an AI-assisted status report
journeys.goal: Produce a professional project status summary from live task, time, and material data, and identify tasks at risk of delay.

steps.title: Open project detail
steps.intent: The project manager navigates to the project detail page to review current task, time log, and material activity before generating a report.

steps.title: Generate status report
steps.intent: The project manager clicks the generate status report button so the system uses LLM to create a professional summary from tasks, time logs, and materials.

steps.title: Review delay-risk suggestions
steps.intent: The project manager reviews the AI-suggested tasks at risk of delay so they can take corrective action before deadlines slip.

steps.title: Share report with client
steps.intent: The project manager shares the generated status report with the client so the client stays informed about project progress.

journeys.outcome: A professional status report is generated, delay-risk tasks are flagged, and the report is shared with the client for communication.
businessRules: Status report content is generated from live project tasks, time logs, and material usage via the platform LLM proxy.
Delay-risk suggestions are advisory and do not automatically change task status.
The project manager can review and edit the report before sharing with the client.

journeys.title: View assigned tasks for the day
journeys.goal: See which tasks are assigned and due so the field worker knows what to work on today.

steps.title: Check today's tasks
steps.intent: The field worker opens the app on their mobile device to see tasks assigned to them so they know what work is expected today.

steps.title: Review task details
steps.intent: The field worker reads the task description and due date so they understand the scope and urgency of each assigned task.

journeys.outcome: The field worker has a clear list of assigned tasks with descriptions and due dates, ready to begin work.
businessRules: Field workers see only tasks assigned to them.
Tasks are sorted by due date to surface the most urgent work first.
The mobile experience must be usable in the field without desktop access.

journeys.title: Log daily time, materials, and task progress
journeys.goal: Record hours worked, materials used, and task completion status so job costing and project tracking stay accurate.

steps.title: Select the task being worked on
steps.intent: The field worker selects the task they are currently working on so their time and material entries are attributed to the correct work item.

steps.title: Log hours worked
steps.intent: The field worker enters the hours spent on the task so labor costs are captured for job costing and progress tracking.

steps.title: Log materials used
steps.intent: The field worker records materials consumed on the task so material costs are attributed to the project for accurate job costing.

steps.title: Update task status
steps.intent: The field worker updates the task status to reflect progress or completion so the project manager and dashboard reflect current field reality.

journeys.outcome: Time logs, material usage, and task status are recorded against the project, keeping job costing and project tracking up to date.
businessRules: Time logs must be linked to a specific task and worker.
Material usage is recorded per project for job costing, not as warehouse stock management.
Task status can only be updated by the assigned worker or the project manager.

journeys.title: Prepare a client billing summary
journeys.goal: Compile accumulated job costs into a clear client-facing billing summary so the client understands what they are being charged for.

steps.title: Review accumulated job costs
steps.intent: The billing staff reviews labor, material, and approved change order costs for the project so they have an accurate cost basis for billing.

steps.title: Compile billing summary
steps.intent: The billing staff assembles a client-facing billing summary that breaks down labor, materials, and change orders so the client can see a clear cost narrative.

steps.title: Share billing summary with client
steps.intent: The billing staff sends the billing summary to the client so the client can review charges before an invoice is generated.

journeys.outcome: A clear billing summary with labor, material, and change order breakdowns is prepared and shared with the client.
businessRules: Billing summaries include only approved change orders.
Job costs are derived from time logs, material usage, and approved change orders.
Billing summaries are client-facing and exclude internal cost-code detail.

journeys.title: Generate an invoice from approved costs
journeys.goal: Create an invoice from approved job costs and change orders so the client receives a formal billing document.

steps.title: Select approved costs
steps.intent: The billing staff selects the approved job costs and change orders to include so the invoice reflects only verified and approved charges.

steps.title: Create the invoice
steps.intent: The billing staff generates an invoice document from the selected costs so the client has a formal billing record.

steps.title: Review and send to client
steps.intent: The billing staff reviews the invoice for accuracy and sends it to the client so billing is communicated and ready for external accounting.

journeys.outcome: An invoice is generated from approved costs and change orders and sent to the client for payment processing outside the system.
businessRules: Invoices are billing documents for construction job costing; payment capture and full accounting remain external.
Only approved change orders can be included in an invoice.
An invoice must reference the project and client.

journeys.title: Receive and review a project status report
journeys.goal: Stay informed about project progress, budget status, and task completion without needing access to internal operations.

steps.title: Receive status report
steps.intent: The client receives a project status report shared by the project manager so they are kept up to date on how their project is progressing.

steps.title: Review progress summary
steps.intent: The client reads the progress summary covering tasks completed, budget status, and upcoming milestones so they have confidence in the project trajectory.

journeys.outcome: The client has a clear, professional view of project progress and budget status without needing internal system access.
businessRules: Clients receive shared status reports; they do not have full internal project editing access.
Status reports are generated and shared by the project manager.
Client visibility is limited to status and billing communication surfaces.

journeys.title: Review a billing summary and invoice
journeys.goal: Review charges for labor, materials, and change orders so the client understands and can approve payment.

steps.title: Receive billing summary
steps.intent: The client receives a billing summary from the billing staff so they can review the cost breakdown before receiving a formal invoice.

steps.title: Review charges
steps.intent: The client reviews the labor, material, and change order charges so they understand what they are paying for and can raise any questions.

journeys.outcome: The client has reviewed the billing summary and invoice, understands the charges, and is ready to process payment externally.
businessRules: Clients see billing summaries and invoices shared by billing staff.
Payment processing and full accounting are handled outside the system.
Clients cannot edit or create billing documents.

features.title: Project lifecycle management
features.description: Create and manage construction projects with client, site address, status, budget, and schedule dates.
features.rationale: Foundation for all other capabilities — without projects, no tasks, costs, or billing can exist.

features.title: Work task assignment and tracking
features.description: Create work tasks tied to projects, assign them to field workers with due dates, and track status through completion.
features.rationale: Core coordination loop between PMs and field crews; drives daily field activity and progress visibility.

features.title: Operational dashboard
features.description: Dashboard showing active projects, budget vs actual signals, and upcoming or overdue tasks across all jobs.
features.rationale: Gives the PM a single pane of glass to spot budget drift and task urgency across multiple projects.

features.title: Project detail with Gantt-ish timeline
features.description: Project detail page with task list and simple timeline-style progress visualization for schedule coordination.
features.rationale: Provides visual schedule context without the complexity of full CPM or critical-path scheduling.

features.title: Labor time logging
features.description: Field workers log hours worked against specific tasks for labor cost tracking and progress visibility.
features.rationale: Labor cost is a primary job costing component; accurate time logs drive budget vs actual accuracy.

features.title: Material usage tracking
features.description: Record materials consumed against projects for job costing, not full warehouse management.
features.rationale: Material costs are a major job costing component; per-project usage tracking keeps cost visibility accurate.

features.title: Change order management
features.description: Create, review cost impact, and approve change orders that adjust scope, cost, or schedule on active projects.
features.rationale: Change orders are inevitable in construction; capturing them formally prevents budget drift and billing disputes.

features.title: Job costing aggregation
features.description: Derive budget vs actual from labor time, material usage, and approved change orders for cost visibility.
features.rationale: Central to the module's value proposition — unifying cost signals that are typically tracked in disconnected ways.

features.title: AI-assisted status report generation
features.description: Generate a professional project status summary from tasks, time logs, and materials using the platform LLM proxy.
features.rationale: Saves PM time and improves client communication quality by auto-summarizing live project data.

features.title: AI delay-risk suggestions
features.description: Suggest tasks at risk of delay based on project activity, due dates, and progress signals via the platform LLM proxy.
features.rationale: Proactive risk identification helps PMs intervene before deadlines slip, improving on-time delivery.

features.title: Client billing summary
features.description: Compile client-facing billing summaries with labor, material, and change order breakdowns from approved job costs.
features.rationale: Bridges job costing and client communication; gives clients a clear cost narrative before invoicing.

features.title: Invoice generation
features.description: Generate formal invoices from approved job costs and change orders for client billing; payment rails remain external.
features.rationale: Formal billing document for construction job costing; bounds invoice complexity to billing summaries, not full accounting.

features.title: Client status report view
features.description: Shared status report surface where clients receive and review project progress, budget, and milestone summaries.
features.rationale: Keeps clients informed without giving them internal editing access; supports the client communication focus.

features.title: Client billing view
features.description: Shared billing surface where clients receive and review billing summaries and invoices.
features.rationale: Gives clients visibility into charges so they can review and approve payment; complements the billing summary and invoice features.
